scenarios.name: AI Startup
scenarios.description: Scrappy AI SaaS with exposed prompt config, debug env data, and a leaky support search.

scenarios.name: Indie SaaS
scenarios.description: Solo-founder SaaS that exposes account data, billing config, client-trusted subscription upgrades, and a dashboard without auth.

scenarios.name: Hosting Panel Bypass
scenarios.description: Hosting control panel that simulates a 2026-style session-loading authentication bypass on internet-exposed admin paths.

scenarios.name: Enterprise Legacy
scenarios.description: Old internal stack with forgotten APIs, direct SQL dumps, and reports behind weak assumptions.

scenarios.name: Supabase Clone
scenarios.description: Project dashboard that loads profiles and storage metadata with an exposed anon config.

scenarios.name: Naked Postgres
scenarios.description: Database console that simulates a publicly reachable Postgres service with weak network and auth settings.

scenarios.name: Next.js App
scenarios.description: A modern frontend that advertises hidden flags and exposes build artifacts.

scenarios.name: GraphQL API
scenarios.description: GraphQL endpoint with enabled introspection and sensitive fields accessible to anonymous callers.

scenarios.name: Fintech App
scenarios.description: Wallet UI that preloads another customer account and accepts weak amount validation.

scenarios.name: Ecommerce Advanced
scenarios.description: Checkout flow that trusts client totals, weak email validation, and exposed order lookups.

scenarios.name: DevOps Leak
scenarios.description: Operations panel with deploy workflow files, verbose logs, and a downloadable backup archive.

scenarios.name: Poisoned CI Action
scenarios.description: Release pipeline that simulates compromised automation credentials, retagged actions, and leaked workflow secrets.

scenarios.name: Staging Env
scenarios.description: Staging UI that automatically loads internal users and skips normal gatekeeping.

scenarios.name: CORS Misconfig
scenarios.description: API playground that highlights a permissive credentialed CORS policy.

scenarios.name: Mobile Backend
scenarios.description: Backend docs that encourage trusting mobile headers and exposing versioned admin APIs.

scenarios.name: Multi Tenant SaaS
scenarios.description: Tenant switcher that happily loads users from another org when the ID changes.

scenarios.name: CMS Platform
scenarios.description: Simple editorial dashboard that stores unsafe HTML and reflects form preview content back into raw HTML.

scenarios.name: Auth System
scenarios.description: Login panel with weak email validation, reusable tokens, and a leaked signing secret.

scenarios.name: Internal Tools
scenarios.description: No-login operations console with internal APIs and support shortcuts rendered on load.

scenarios.name: Analytics Dashboard
scenarios.description: Open metrics board that fetches revenue and customer health data on first paint.

scenarios.name: File Upload Service
scenarios.description: Upload widget that accepts arbitrary names, weak content checks, and traversal-style reads.

scenarios.name: Chat App
scenarios.description: Shared chat room that stores raw HTML and leaks other room traffic into the default view.

scenarios.name: Config Leak
scenarios.description: Settings page that loads environment, feature flags, and internal hostnames into the browser.

scenarios.name: Git Exposed
scenarios.description: Minimal site whose public surface includes live repository metadata files.

scenarios.name: Feature Flag App
scenarios.description: Frontend boot script enables admin and bypass flows before the server checks anything.

scenarios.name: Hybrid Modern App
scenarios.description: Calibration target with intentionally mixed results so scanners can measure precision as well as recall.

scenarios.name: Agent Tool Abuse
scenarios.description: Chat agent concatenates user input into the system prompt and exposes shell, fetch, and fs tools that anyone can drive.

scenarios.name: RAG Poisoning
scenarios.description: Knowledge base accepts public uploads and treats poisoned chunks as authoritative answers.

scenarios.name: Open MCP Server
scenarios.description: Internet-reachable MCP server with no auth that exposes shell.exec, db.query, and secrets.read.

scenarios.name: Vector DB Leak
scenarios.description: Frontend ships a Pinecone key and the search endpoint accepts a wildcard namespace across tenants.

scenarios.name: OAuth Redirect
scenarios.description: OAuth authorize endpoint trusts arbitrary redirect_uri values and never verifies state or PKCE.

scenarios.name: Password Reset Flaws
scenarios.description: Reset flow leaks account existence, ships tokens in URLs, and accepts predictable 6-digit values.

scenarios.name: JWT Alg Confusion
scenarios.description: Verifier accepts alg=none and dereferences attacker-controlled kid paths.

scenarios.name: Magic Link & OTP
scenarios.description: Passwordless flow with no rate limit, 6-digit OTP, and reusable long-TTL magic links.

scenarios.name: SSRF Image Proxy
scenarios.description: Avatar resizer fetches arbitrary URLs including cloud metadata, internal services, and file://.

scenarios.name: Raw SQL Injection
scenarios.description: User search builds SQL by string concatenation and reflects errors back to the client.

scenarios.name: NoSQL Operator Injection
scenarios.description: Login passes JSON sub-objects into Mongo so $ne/$gt operators bypass authentication.

scenarios.name: Server-Side Template Injection
scenarios.description: Newsletter previewer evaluates user-supplied templates with access to env globals.

scenarios.name: Mass Assignment
scenarios.description: Profile PATCH spreads request body into the user record and lets clients write is_admin.

scenarios.name: Open Redirect
scenarios.description: Login callback honors any next URL, including protocol-relative and javascript: payloads.

scenarios.name: XXE in SVG
scenarios.description: SVG parser resolves external entities and embeds their contents into the rendered output.

scenarios.name: Zip Slip
scenarios.description: Archive importer writes entries using their raw filenames, escaping the upload directory.

scenarios.name: Webhook Unverified
scenarios.description: Stripe and GitHub webhook handlers skip signature checks or use weak ==.

scenarios.name: Stripe Paid-Param Trust
scenarios.description: Checkout success page upgrades plans based on URL query params instead of verifying with Stripe.

scenarios.name: Swagger UI Exposed
scenarios.description: Swagger UI is reachable with a pre-filled bearer token and lists every admin endpoint.

scenarios.name: Sentry / Telemetry Keys
scenarios.description: Frontend bundle exposes Sentry DSN, PostHog write key, and Datadog client token.

scenarios.name: Prototype Pollution
scenarios.description: Deep-merge endpoint walks __proto__ keys, polluting global config and feature flags.

scenarios.name: postMessage No Origin
scenarios.description: Parent page accepts postMessage events from any origin and runs privileged actions.

scenarios.name: Missing CSP / Headers
scenarios.description: Responses ship without CSP, X-Frame-Options, or HSTS, enabling framing and inline scripts.

scenarios.name: CSRF Missing
scenarios.description: Email change form has no CSRF token and the session cookie is set with SameSite=None.

scenarios.name: Public S3 Bucket
scenarios.description: User-content bucket grants ListBucket and PutObject to wildcard principal.

scenarios.name: Subdomain Takeover
scenarios.description: Marketing subdomain CNAMEs to a deleted Heroku app and is claimable by anyone.

scenarios.name: Open Redis
scenarios.description: Redis bound to 0.0.0.0:6379 with no requirepass, leaking sessions and live commands.

scenarios.name: Open MongoDB
scenarios.description: MongoDB bound publicly with --noauth, exposing tenant DBs and password hashes.

scenarios.name: ref0 (Clean Reference)
scenarios.description: Clean reference site with auth required, validated input, secure cookies, and full security headers. Any finding here is a false positive.

scenarios.name: Agent Confused Deputy
scenarios.description: Agent uses caller's bearer token but operates on an as_user param without authorization checks.

scenarios.name: Indirect Prompt Injection
scenarios.description: Agent fetches user-supplied URLs and follows hidden instructions embedded in the page content.

scenarios.name: LLM Output as HTML
scenarios.description: Frontend renders model output via innerHTML, executing any HTML the model emits.

scenarios.name: HTTP Request Smuggling
scenarios.description: Front and back proxies disagree on Content-Length vs Transfer-Encoding, smuggling hidden requests.

scenarios.name: CRLF Response Splitting
scenarios.description: User input is reflected into Location without stripping CRLF, allowing extra headers.

scenarios.name: Cache Poisoning
scenarios.description: Origin reflects X-Forwarded-Host into the body but the CDN omits it from the cache key.

scenarios.name: Regex DoS
scenarios.description: Validator regex backtracks exponentially in input length, allowing CPU pegging.

scenarios.name: Insecure Deserialization
scenarios.description: Importer pipes user bytes into pickle.loads and accepts polymorphic Jackson types.

scenarios.name: TLS Downgrade
scenarios.description: Sensitive paths over HTTP, TLS 1.0 with RC4, expired certificate, no HSTS.

scenarios.name: Weak Randomness
scenarios.description: Tokens derived from math/rand seeded by Unix seconds; sequential output is predictable.

scenarios.name: Cookie Scope Leak
scenarios.description: Session cookie set with Domain=.example.com travels to every subdomain including third-party hosts.

scenarios.name: Download Path Traversal
scenarios.description: Download endpoint joins user filename into base path without normalization.

scenarios.name: LDAP Injection
scenarios.description: Directory search builds LDAP filters by string concatenation, allowing wildcard matches.

scenarios.name: XPath Injection
scenarios.description: Legacy XML auth concatenates user input into the XPath query, enabling tautology bypass.

scenarios.name: Email MIME Injection
scenarios.description: Contact form passes subject into SMTP headers without stripping CRLF, allowing Bcc injection.

scenarios.name: DOM Clobbering
scenarios.description: Boot script reads window.config but a comment-stored form with name="config" clobbers it.

scenarios.name: DOM Fragment XSS
scenarios.description: Banner reads location.hash and writes it via innerHTML, executing fragment payloads.

scenarios.name: PDF HTML Injection
scenarios.description: Invoice PDF generator interpolates user input into HTML with file:// access enabled.

scenarios.name: Markdown HTML Injection
scenarios.description: Markdown renderer keeps sanitize:false so embedded HTML and scripts reach the page.

scenarios.name: OAuth Token via Referer
scenarios.description: Callback page loads a third-party CDN script while access tokens sit in the URL fragment.

scenarios.name: PKCE Downgrade
scenarios.description: Token endpoint accepts authorization codes without verifying code_verifier.

scenarios.name: Weak Password Policy
scenarios.description: Signup accepts 5-character passwords with no breach check and a global rate limit.

scenarios.name: Audit Log Tamper
scenarios.description: Audit writer accepts client-supplied timestamps and actor IDs and never escapes newlines.

scenarios.name: GCP Metadata SSRF
scenarios.description: Proxy reaches GCP and Azure metadata services and returns service-account tokens.

scenarios.name: Open Kubernetes Dashboard
scenarios.description: Dashboard uses --enable-skip-login and apiserver permits anonymous list of namespaces and secrets.

scenarios.name: gRPC Reflection Enabled
scenarios.description: Production gRPC server registers the reflection service, exposing admin RPCs and field shapes.

scenarios.name: WebSocket No Origin Check
scenarios.description: Upgrade handler accepts any Origin and cookies travel on the upgrade.

scenarios.name: DNS Rebinding
scenarios.description: Local-only admin gates by Host: localhost; a 5s TTL DNS flip lets victim browsers bypass it.

scenarios.name: Clipboard Paste XSS
scenarios.description: Rich paste handler reads text/html from clipboard and writes it via innerHTML.

scenarios.name: Prompt Leak via Error
scenarios.description: 500 responses include the rendered prompt, retrieved chunks, and stack traces.

scenarios.name: Tool Output Injection
scenarios.description: Agent feeds tool output back into prompt, so tool results containing instructions hijack the loop.

scenarios.name: Function-Calling Arg Poison
scenarios.description: Function-calling schema accepts free-form strings the backend interpolates into SQL or exec.

scenarios.name: Session Fixation
scenarios.description: Login keeps the pre-auth session ID, so an attacker-planted cookie remains valid post-login.

scenarios.name: Email Change No Reauth
scenarios.description: Email change requires only a session, then password reset goes to the new email.

scenarios.name: Host Header Injection
scenarios.description: Reset mailer builds the link from the inbound Host header with no allow-list.

scenarios.name: Open Elasticsearch
scenarios.description: Elasticsearch with security disabled exposes _cat/indices and _search across tenants.

scenarios.name: Open Firebase Rules
scenarios.description: Firebase realtime rules set to .read/.write true, allowing anonymous dump and overwrite.

scenarios.name: Weak JWT Secret
scenarios.description: HS256 secret is the literal word 'secret', shared across staging and production.

scenarios.name: Race-Condition Balance
scenarios.description: Read-decide-write withdraw without a transaction lets concurrent requests both succeed.

scenarios.name: ref-oauth (Clean Reference)
scenarios.description: Reference OAuth flow with exact-match redirect_uri, required state, and enforced PKCE.

scenarios.name: ref-jwt (Clean Reference)
scenarios.description: Reference JWT verifier with RS256 only, kid allow-list, and rejection of alg=none/HS256.

scenarios.name: ref-webhook (Clean Reference)
scenarios.description: Reference Stripe webhook with required signature, constant-time HMAC compare, per-env secret.

scenarios.name: ref-rls (Clean Reference)
scenarios.description: Reference Supabase-style profiles endpoint with row-level security enforced server-side.

scenarios.name: NPM Typosquat
scenarios.description: package.json depends on a typo of a popular package whose preinstall script exfiltrates env vars.

scenarios.name: Docker Config Leak
scenarios.description: Web root serves ~/.docker/config.json, leaking registry credentials and helper-store metadata.

scenarios.name: Terraform State Leak
scenarios.description: S3 bucket holding terraform.tfstate is publicly readable, exposing inline secrets and resource layout.

scenarios.name: MCP Tool Spec Injection
scenarios.description: MCP client trusts tool descriptions from a third-party server, which embed hidden instructions the agent obeys.

scenarios.name: Noisy Errors
scenarios.description: Bootstrap returns 500/503/404/malformed JSON and the page emits console.error and a thrown JS exception. Robustness check, not a vulnerability.

scenarios.name: Captcha / Bot Challenge
scenarios.description: Cloudflare-style interstitial with __cf_bm and cf_clearance cookies, Turnstile-like widget, and content that only settles after JS runs.
